Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run set for spring 2027. It will be her first full tour of the region since she stepped away from performing in 2025. Since returning, she has chosen one-off shows and festival appearances instead of immediately rebuilding the schedule she cancelled. The new dates mark the point where that gradual return turns back into a sustained run of headline shows.

The break began after she collapsed during her set at All Things Go in New York and then cancelled her remaining performances for the foreseeable future. In the message that followed, she said she needed time to work on herself and asked listeners to give her "a second chance" when she was ready to return. She gave no timetable for coming back. When she eventually returned, it was through individual appearances rather than a replacement for the North American tour built around *I'm Only F**king Myself*.

At the Grammys, "Messy" won Best Pop Solo Performance, her first Grammy, and she performed the song during the ceremony. Headline shows in Britain and festival appearances followed. She later returned to All Things Go, the same festival where the previous run had ended abruptly. By the time the 2027 dates were announced, she had already spent months performing again across very different settings. What she had not yet done was commit to another full North American run.

[apple:song:6768357139:6768357142]

"From Down Here" arrived during that period, her first new music since *I'm Only F**king Myself*. She has said the idea hit the day after the Grammys and led her into the studio with James Blake. She described the song as missing an old high while knowing that a more grounded life is safer and more rewarding. The music is calmer than much of the album, but the writing remains blunt about the pull of the life she is trying to leave behind.

The tour name, "Everything Begins," flips the wording of her "Everything Ends" tattoo. When she cancelled the rest of her shows in 2025, she asked fans for "a second chance" after taking time to work on herself. The new run is the first full North American schedule she has committed to since that message. After rebuilding her live work through individual shows and festivals, she is returning to the multiweek touring format that disappeared from her calendar when she stepped away.
